Ertugrul: Turkish, from er 'man, brave' and tugrul 'falcon', so 'brave falcon'. Father of Osman I, founder of the Ottoman dynasty.
Macy: English, from a surname from the French place Massy, from Latin Maccius. Also used as a short form of Mercy.
Ramy: Arabic Rami, meaning 'archer, one who throws'.
Vinny: English and Italian short form of Vincent, from Latin vincens 'conquering'.
Maëlie: Probably a French blend of Maëlle (Breton 'prince, chief') and Amélie. Origin uncertain.
Neela: Sanskrit and Hindi, meaning 'blue' or 'dark blue'.
Thias: Short form of Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Anja: Slavic and German form of Anna, from Hebrew Hannah, 'grace'.
Bahar: Turkish and Persian, meaning 'spring' the season.
Hafssa: Arabic Hafsa, meaning 'young lioness'. A wife of Muhammad was named Hafsa.
Loran: Variant of Lauren or Lorent, from Latin Laurentius, 'from Laurentum'. Also Breton 'laurel'.
Marie-Alix: French compound of Marie (Hebrew Miriam) and Alix, from Germanic Adalheid 'noble kind'.
Nisanur: Turkish, from Nisan 'April' and nur 'light', so 'light of April'.
Preston: English, from a place name meaning 'priest's farm'. Originally a surname.
Sabina: Latin, 'woman of the Sabines', an ancient Italic people.
Sefora: Italian and Spanish form of Zipporah, Hebrew for 'bird'. Wife of Moses.
Elisha: Hebrew Elisha, 'God is salvation'. A biblical prophet; as a girl's name a variant of Elise or Alicia.
Malena: Spanish short form of Magdalena, from Hebrew-Greek 'of Magdala'. Also Slavic and Scandinavian use.
Monika: Slavic and German form of Monica, possibly from Latin moneo 'to advise'. Origin uncertain; Saint Monica's name is likely Berber.
Tiara: From the English word for a jewelled crown, from Greek tiara. A modern given name.
Yael: Hebrew, meaning 'ibex' or 'mountain goat'. A biblical heroine.
Zacharia: Variant of Zachariah, Hebrew Zekharyah, 'God remembers'. Also the Arabic Zakariya.
Alek: Short form of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'. Used across Slavic and English languages.
Alisia: Variant of Alicia or Alyssa, from Germanic Adalheid 'noble kind'. Origin partly uncertain.
Carsten: Low German form of Christian, from Greek christianos 'follower of Christ'.
Keren: Hebrew, meaning 'horn' or 'ray of light'. Short for Keren-happuch in the Bible. Also Celtic Keren.
Ainhoa: Basque, from a Marian shrine at Ainhoa. The name's meaning is uncertain, possibly 'place of wild herbs'.
Arzu: Turkish, from Persian arzu, meaning 'wish, desire'.
Celya: Variant of Celia, from Latin Caelia 'heavenly', or Cecilia 'blind'. Origin uncertain.
Darren: English and Irish, perhaps from Irish Dáire or Ó Dorain, 'great'. Modern given name of uncertain origin.
Eddy: English short form of Edward or Edwin, from Old English ead 'wealth' and weard 'guardian'.
Claudio: Italian and Spanish form of Claudius, from Latin claudus 'lame', a Roman clan name.
Eloy: Spanish and French (Éloi), from Latin eligere 'to choose', so 'chosen'.
Kaylie: Modern English variant of Kayla or Kylie, of Hebrew or Aboriginal origin. Origin uncertain.
Séraphine: French, from Hebrew seraph 'burning one', an angel of the highest order.
Armando: Italian and Spanish form of Herman, from Germanic hariman 'army man'.
Céléna: Variant of Selena or Celina, from Greek Selene 'moon' or Latin caelum 'sky'. Origin uncertain.
Pixie: English word for a mythical fairy of Cornwall and Devon. Modern given name.
Ylano: Modern coined name, probably a variant of Milan or Eliano. Origin uncertain.
Youcef: Maghrebi Arabic form of Yusuf (Joseph), Hebrew 'God will add'.
India: From the country, whose name comes from the Indus river, Sanskrit sindhu 'river'.
Karol: Polish and Slovak form of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Kelyan: Modern Breton-style name, possibly a blend of Kelly and Yan. Origin uncertain.
Pelle: Scandinavian short form of Peter, from Greek petros 'rock'.
Xenne: Probably a modern Dutch variant of Xenia or Xander, Greek 'hospitality' or 'defender'. Origin uncertain.
Anabelle: English, a blend of Anna and Belle, or Amabel from Latin amabilis 'lovable'.
Greg: English short form of Gregory, from Greek gregorios 'watchful'.
Henrik: Scandinavian and Hungarian form of Henry, from Germanic heim 'home' and rik 'ruler'.
Jolene: American, probably a blend of Jo and the ending -lene. Popularised by Dolly Parton's song.
Juliano: Italian and Portuguese form of Julian, from Latin Julianus, from the clan Julius.
Nyssa: Greek, meaning 'goal' or 'new beginning', or a town in myth. Also a type of tree.
Maïthé: Probably a French variant of Maïté or Maite, Basque 'beloved' or Spanish Maria Teresa. Origin uncertain.
Nout: Dutch short form of Arnout (Arnold), from Germanic arn 'eagle' and wald 'rule'.
Teoman: Turkish, from Teoman, the first Xiongnu ruler, also called Modu. Meaning uncertain, linked to 'ten thousand'.
Carlotta: Italian form of Charlotte, feminine of Charles, from Germanic karl 'free man'.
Ciel: French, meaning 'sky, heaven'. Rare given name.
Jeremiah: Hebrew Yirmeyahu, usually 'God will raise up' or 'God exalts'. A biblical prophet.
Lou-Ann: French compound of Lou (Louis or Louise) and Ann, from Hebrew Hannah 'grace'.
Mauritz: Dutch and Scandinavian form of Maurice, from Latin Mauritius, 'dark-skinned, Moorish'.
Badreddine: Arabic Badr al-Din, 'full moon of the faith'.
Eowyn: Created by J. R. R. Tolkien in The Lord of the Rings, from Old English eoh 'horse' and wynn 'joy'.
Eyüp: Turkish form of Ayyub, Arabic for Job, the biblical figure of patience.
Fernando: Spanish and Portuguese, from Germanic Ferdinand, 'bold journey' or 'brave voyager'.
Huseyin: Turkish form of Husayn, Arabic diminutive of hasan, meaning 'handsome, good'.
Rina: Short form of names ending -rina, such as Katrina or Marina. Hebrew Rina means 'joy, song'.
Sus: Dutch short form of Susanna, from Hebrew shoshanna 'lily, rose'. Occasionally used for boys.
Xandro: Short form of Alexandro, from Greek Alexandros, 'defender of men'.
Caithlyn: Variant of Caitlin, Irish form of Catherine, from Greek Aikaterine 'pure'.
Ianthe: Greek, from ion 'violet' and anthos 'flower'. A name in myth, used by poets.
Liena: Possibly a variant of Lina, Lena or Liene, as in Latvian 'Liene'. Origin uncertain.
Maddox: Welsh and English, from Welsh Madog 'fortunate' with 'son of'.
Savana: Variant of Savannah, from a Taino word for a treeless plain.
Sevan: Armenian, from Lake Sevan, perhaps 'black monastery'. Also Turkish 'one who loves'.
Sherine: Arabic Shirin, from Persian shirin 'sweet'. Also a variant of Shirin and Sharon.
Younès: Arabic Yunus, Jonah, from Hebrew yonah 'dove'.
Alexie: French variant of Alexis, from Greek alexios 'helper, defender'.
Maéline: Probably a French blend of Maëlle and Éline, or from Madeleine. Origin uncertain.
Meghan: Welsh form of Megan, a diminutive of Margaret, from Greek margarites 'pearl'.
Mirre: Dutch and Frisian, probably a variant of Mirre, from Mirjam, or from Dutch mirre 'myrrh'. Origin uncertain.
Sefa: Turkish, from Arabic safa, meaning 'purity, joy'. In Finnish used for Seppo.
Ylias: Variant of Elias, Greek form of Elijah, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Alysia: Variant of Alicia or Alyssa, from Germanic Adalheid 'noble kind'. Possibly influenced by Greek alysson 'madwort'.
Florie: French diminutive of Florence, from Latin florens 'blossoming'.
Macha: Russian diminutive of Maria, from Hebrew Miriam. Also an Irish Celtic goddess of war.
Mélody: French form of Melody, from Greek melodia 'singing of songs'.
Ylian: Variant of Julian or Elian, from Latin Julianus or Hebrew 'my God'. Origin uncertain.
Cerise: French, meaning 'cherry'. Also the colour name.
Ekrem: Turkish, from Arabic Akram, meaning 'most generous, honourable'.
Hailie: Modern English variant of Hayley, from an Old English place name 'hay clearing'.
Johanne: Scandinavian and French feminine of Johannes, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Jorbe: Probably a Flemish short form of Jorben or Joris. Joris is a Dutch form of George 'farmer'. Origin uncertain.
Maïwenn: Breton, from mai 'dear' or 'Mary' and gwenn 'white, blessed'.
Suzon: French diminutive of Suzanne, from Hebrew shoshanna 'lily'.
Akin: Turkish, meaning 'raid, rush, flow'. Also Yoruba 'brave'.
Annalisa: Italian compound of Anna and Lisa, from Hebrew 'grace' and 'God is an oath'.
Elsie: Scottish diminutive of Elspeth or Elizabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Havva: Turkish form of Eve, from Hebrew Chavah, 'life' or 'living'.
Lenna: Probably a variant of Lena or Helena, from Greek 'torch'. Also a Swedish form.
Mélyne: Probably a French variant of Mélina, from Greek meli 'honey'. Origin uncertain.
Riana: Possibly a variant of Rhiannon, a Welsh goddess, or Rianne, from Marianne. Origin uncertain.
Safya: Arabic Safiya, meaning 'pure, sincere friend'. A wife of Muhammad.
Tias: Short form of Matthias or Tobias, Hebrew 'gift of God' and 'God is good'.
Anaelle: French, a blend of Anna and Elle, or from Breton Anaïs. Origin uncertain.
Christos: Greek, meaning 'anointed one', from christos. Greek form of the name Christ.
Lone: Danish, short form of Abelone or Magdalone, linked to Hebrew 'of Magdala'. Origin partly uncertain.
Alonzo: Spanish form of Alfonso, from Germanic adal 'noble' and funs 'ready'.
Isalie: Probably a variant of Isaline or Elisabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'. Origin uncertain.
Israel: Hebrew, 'he struggles with God' or 'God contends'. Given to Jacob in the Bible.
Joan: Catalan and English form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'. In Dutch used for girls.
Leart: Albanian, from lear meaning 'to be free', so 'free'. A modern name.
Lorédana: Probably a Romance variant of Loredana, Italian, perhaps from Laura or Loreto. Origin uncertain.
Meredith: Welsh, from Maredudd, 'great lord' or 'sea protector', used for both sexes.
Michal: Czech and Polish form of Michael; Hebrew Michal 'who is like God?'. In Hebrew it is a girl's name.
Stanley: English, from a place name meaning 'stony clearing'. Originally a surname.
Almina: Bosnian and Latin, probably from Arabic al-amina, 'the trustworthy'. Origin uncertain.
Arnold: Germanic, from arn 'eagle' and wald 'power, rule'.
Aïssa: Arabic, a form of Issa (Jesus) or of Aisha 'alive, living'. Origin varies; common in Africa and Belgium.
Catarina: Portuguese and Italian form of Katherine, from Greek Aikaterine, of uncertain origin.
Indi: Probably a short form of India or Indigo, or a Romani name. Origin uncertain.
Maïssane: Probably a variant of Maysan or Maissa, Arabic 'walking proudly'. Origin uncertain.
Noore: Dutch variant of Noor, Arabic nur 'light'.
Rayana: Arabic Rayyana, meaning 'beautiful and fresh'. Also Hebrew for 'friend'.
Timoté: French form of Timothy, from Greek timotheos 'honouring God'.
Barnabé: French form of Barnabas, Aramaic 'son of encouragement' or 'son of the prophet'.
Gian: Italian and Romansh short form of Giovanni, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Irène: French form of Irene, from Greek eirene 'peace'.
Lemmy: English diminutive, famous as the nickname of Motörhead's Lemmy Kilmister. Possibly from 'Lemuel' or 'lemme'.
Mohamed-Amin: Arabic compound of Muhammad 'praised' and Amin 'trustworthy, faithful'.
Alpay: Turkish, from alp 'hero' and ay 'moon', so 'brave hero'.
Elaine: French form of Helen, from Greek 'torch'. In Arthurian legend, Elaine of Astolat.
Gabryel: Variant of Gabriel, Hebrew 'God is my strength'.
Mathies: Dutch variant of Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Maxwell: Scottish, from Maxwell, a place name meaning 'Maccus's stream'. Originally a surname.
Mimoun: Arabic Maymun, meaning 'blessed, fortunate'. Common in Morocco.
Mitte: Probably a Frisian or Dutch short form of Mathilde or Mirte. Origin uncertain.
Abigaïl: French form of Abigail, Hebrew 'my father is joy'. Wife of David in the Bible.
Aileen: Scottish and Irish form of Eileen, possibly from Helen 'torch'.
Alyzée: French variant of Alizé, meaning 'trade wind'.
Amely: Variant of Amelie or Amélie, from Germanic amal 'work'. Often confused with Latin Aemilia.
Lili-Rose: French compound of Lili, from Elisabeth or lily, and Rose, from Germanic hros or Latin rosa.
Abdelrahman: Arabic Abd al-Rahman, 'servant of the Merciful', one of God's names.
Andi: Short form of Andreas or Andrew, Greek 'manly'. Also Albanian Andi.
Elioth: Probably a variant of Elliott or Elio, from Hebrew Elijah, or Greek helios 'sun'. Origin uncertain.
Farouk: Arabic Faruq, meaning 'one who distinguishes truth from falsehood'.
Noëmi: Variant of Naomi, Hebrew 'pleasantness'. Common in German and Swiss use.
Romaisa: Arabic Rumaysa, a Companion's name, probably from a word for a small sweet-smelling plant. Origin uncertain.
Solange: French, from Latin Sollemnia, 'solemn, dignified'. A French saint.
Veronika: Slavic and German form of Veronica, from Latin vera icon 'true image', or Greek Berenike 'bringer of victory'.
Dakota: Native American, from Lakota Dakhóta 'friend, ally'. A modern given name.
Georgios: Greek form of George, from georgos 'farmer'.
Gökhan: Turkish, from gök 'sky, blue' and han 'ruler', so 'sky ruler'.
Lona: Probably a short form of Apollonia or Leonie, or Danish Lone. Origin uncertain.
Marianna: Italian and Slavic form of Marianne, a blend of Maria and Anna.
Alen: Variant of Alan, probably Breton 'little rock' or 'handsome'. Also Slavic.
Ange: French, meaning 'angel', from Greek angelos 'messenger'. Common in Corsica.
Arianne: French form of Ariadne, Greek 'most holy'. Also Welsh Arianrhod 'silver'.
Django: Romani, meaning 'I awake', made famous by guitarist Django Reinhardt. Also a variant of Jean.
Krystian: Polish form of Christian, from Greek christianos 'follower of Christ'.
Zidane: Arabic Zayyan or Zidan, meaning 'increasing' or 'adornment'. Popularised by footballer Zinedine Zidane.
Félicia: French and Latin form of Felicia, from felix 'lucky, happy'.
Lula: Short form of Louise or Lucille, or Arabic lulu 'pearl'. Also Hawaiian.
Léanna: Variant of Leanna, English blend of Lee and Anna, or French Léa 'weary' plus Anna. Origin uncertain.
Naut: Dutch short form of Arnout or Renaut, Germanic names. Origin uncertain.
Paris: From the Greek prince Paris, whose name is of uncertain origin, or from the French city. Mostly girls in Belgium.
Aglaé: French form of Aglaia, Greek for 'splendour, beauty', one of the three Graces.
Daymon: Variant of Damon, from Greek daman 'to tame', or Daemon. Origin uncertain.
Ernesto: Spanish and Italian form of Ernest, from Germanic ernust 'earnestness, serious'.
Joackim: Variant of Joachim, Hebrew 'God will establish'.
Mathyas: Variant of Mathias or Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Zoélie: French blend of Zoé and Élie, Greek zoe 'life'.
Alberto: Italian and Spanish form of Albert, from Germanic adal 'noble' and berht 'bright'.
Bartosz: Polish form of Bartholomew, Aramaic 'son of Talmai', 'furrow'.
Dax: English, from a French town name of Dax, Gascony, or from Gaulish 'water'. Modern given name.
Ilaya: Probably an Indian or modern variant, Tamil 'young'. Or variant of Elaia. Origin uncertain.
Katherine: English form of Greek Aikaterine, of uncertain origin and long linked to katharos 'pure'.
Kélya: Probably a French modern variant of Kelly or Kélia. Origin uncertain.
Lenno: Probably a Dutch variant of Lennart or Lenno, from Germanic leon 'lion'. Origin uncertain.
Loriano: Italian, from Loriano, a derivative of Latin Laurianus, 'of the laurel'. Origin uncertain.
Maceo: Spanish, from a place name or from Portuguese Macedo. Cuban independence general Antonio Maceo. Origin uncertain.
Micha: Short form of Michael or Michaël, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'. Also a Hebrew prophet's name.
Wodan: Germanic, the chief god Wodan or Odin, from Proto-Germanic 'frenzy, fury'. Rare modern revival.
Mallory: English, from Old French maloure 'unfortunate'. Originally a surname.
